questions.q: A galvanometer of resistance $G$ and figure of merit $K$ produces full-scale deflection for $n$ divisions. It is first converted into an ammeter of maximum range $I$ using a shunt resistance $S$. The same galvanometer is then converted into a voltmeter of maximum range $V$ using a series resistance $R$. The ratio of the maximum ranges $\dfrac{V}{I}$ is
questions.question: A galvanometer of resistance $G$ and figure of merit $K$ produces full-scale deflection for $n$ divisions. It is first converted into an ammeter of maximum range $I$ using a shunt resistance $S$. The same galvanometer is then converted into a voltmeter of maximum range $V$ using a series resistance $R$. The ratio of the maximum ranges $\dfrac{V}{I}$ is
questions.solution:
The full-scale deflection current of the galvanometer is $I_G = nK$.

When converted into an ammeter using a shunt resistance $S$, the maximum current range $I$ is given by:
$I_G G = (I - I_G) S$
$I = I_G \dfrac{G+S}{S}$

When converted into a voltmeter using a series resistance $R$, the maximum voltage range $V$ is given by:
$V = I_G (G+R)$

Dividing the expression for $V$ by the expression for $I$, the term $I_G$ cancels out:
$\dfrac{V}{I} = \dfrac{I_G (G+R)}{I_G \dfrac{G+S}{S}}$

$\dfrac{V}{I} = \dfrac{S(G+R)}{G+S}$

Answer: $\dfrac{S(G+R)}{G+S}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Three parallel branches are connected between a common node A and the ground. The first branch consists of a $20\text{ V}$ battery with an internal resistance of $2\Omega$. The second branch consists of a $4\text{ V}$ battery with an internal resistance of $2\Omega$. The third branch consists of a $4\text{ V}$ battery with an internal resistance of $1\Omega$. The positive terminals of all three batteries face node A, and their negative terminals are grounded. The power dissipated in the internal resistance of the $20\text{ V}$ battery is _____ $\text{W}$.
questions.question: Three parallel branches are connected between a common node A and the ground. The first branch consists of a $20\text{ V}$ battery with an internal resistance of $2\Omega$. The second branch consists of a $4\text{ V}$ battery with an internal resistance of $2\Omega$. The third branch consists of a $4\text{ V}$ battery with an internal resistance of $1\Omega$. The positive terminals of all three batteries face node A, and their negative terminals are grounded. The power dissipated in the internal resistance of the $20\text{ V}$ battery is _____ $\text{W}$.
questions.solution:
Let the potential at the common node A be $V_A$.

Using Millman's theorem or Kirchhoff's Current Law, the voltage at node A is given by:

$V_A = \dfrac{\dfrac{E_1}{R_1} + \dfrac{E_2}{R_2} + \dfrac{E_3}{R_3}}{\dfrac{1}{R_1} + \dfrac{1}{R_2} + \dfrac{1}{R_3}}$

$V_A = \dfrac{\dfrac{20}{2} + \dfrac{4}{2} + \dfrac{4}{1}}{\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{1}}$

$V_A = \dfrac{10 + 2 + 4}{0.5 + 0.5 + 1} = \dfrac{16}{2} = 8\text{ V}$

The current $I_1$ flowing through the first branch is:

$I_1 = \dfrac{E_1 - V_A}{R_1} = \dfrac{20 - 8}{2} = \dfrac{12}{2} = 6\text{ A}$

The power dissipated in the internal resistance of the $20\text{ V}$ battery is:

$P = I_1^2 R_1 = (6)^2 \times 2 = 36 \times 2 = 72\text{ W}$

Answer: $72$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A potentiometer circuit is set up with an ideal driver cell of emf $V_0$ (having zero internal resistance) connected directly across a uniform potentiometer wire of length $100 \ \text{cm}$ and resistance $10 \ \Omega$. A given primary cell of emf $E$ is balanced at a length of $60 \ \text{cm}$ from the positive end. If the potentiometer wire is replaced by another uniform wire of the same length but having a resistance of $20 \ \Omega$ (keeping the driver cell unchanged), the new balancing length for the same primary cell will be:
questions.question: A potentiometer circuit is set up with an ideal driver cell of emf $V_0$ (having zero internal resistance) connected directly across a uniform potentiometer wire of length $100 \ \text{cm}$ and resistance $10 \ \Omega$. A given primary cell of emf $E$ is balanced at a length of $60 \ \text{cm}$ from the positive end. If the potentiometer wire is replaced by another uniform wire of the same length but having a resistance of $20 \ \Omega$ (keeping the driver cell unchanged), the new balancing length for the same primary cell will be:
questions.solution:
For a potentiometer, the potential gradient $k$ is the potential difference per unit length of the wire.

Since the driver cell is ideal (zero internal resistance) and is connected directly across the potentiometer wire, the potential difference across the entire wire is always equal to the emf of the driver cell, $V_0$, regardless of the wire's resistance.

The potential gradient in the first case is:
$k_1 = \dfrac{V_0}{100} \ \text{V/cm}$

The balancing length $l_1$ for the primary cell of emf $E$ is:
$E = k_1 l_1 = \left(\dfrac{V_0}{100}\right) \times 60$

When the wire is replaced by one with $20 \ \Omega$ resistance, the potential difference across it remains $V_0$. Thus, the new potential gradient is:
$k_2 = \dfrac{V_0}{100} \ \text{V/cm}$

Since $k_2 = k_1$, the balancing length for the same cell $E$ remains unchanged.

$l_2 = \dfrac{E}{k_2} = 60 \ \text{cm}$

Answer: $60 \ \text{cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two resistors $R_1 = 6 \, \Omega$ and $R_2 = 12 \, \Omega$ are connected in series across an ideal $12 \text{ V}$ battery. A non-ideal voltmeter is first connected across $R_1$ and it reads $3 \text{ V}$. If the same voltmeter is now disconnected from $R_1$ and connected across $R_2$, its reading will be _____ $\text{V}$.
questions.question: Two resistors $R_1 = 6 \, \Omega$ and $R_2 = 12 \, \Omega$ are connected in series across an ideal $12 \text{ V}$ battery. A non-ideal voltmeter is first connected across $R_1$ and it reads $3 \text{ V}$. If the same voltmeter is now disconnected from $R_1$ and connected across $R_2$, its reading will be _____ $\text{V}$.
questions.solution:
Let the resistance of the voltmeter be $R_v$.

Case 1: Voltmeter across $R_1$
The voltage across $R_1$ is $3 \text{ V}$. The remaining voltage from the $12 \text{ V}$ battery drops across $R_2$:
$V_{R2} = 12 - 3 = 9 \text{ V}$
The current through $R_2$ (which is the total current) is:
$I = \dfrac{9}{12} = 0.75 \text{ A}$
The equivalent resistance of the parallel combination of $R_1$ and $R_v$ is:
$R_{p1} = \dfrac{3 \text{ V}}{0.75 \text{ A}} = 4 \, \Omega$
Thus, $\dfrac{6 R_v}{6 + R_v} = 4 \Rightarrow 6 R_v = 24 + 4 R_v \Rightarrow 2 R_v = 24 \Rightarrow R_v = 12 \, \Omega$

Case 2: Voltmeter across $R_2$
The voltmeter is now in parallel with $R_2$. The new equivalent resistance of this parallel branch is:
$R_{p2} = \dfrac{12 \times 12}{12 + 12} = 6 \, \Omega$
The total resistance of the circuit is now:
$R_{eq} = R_1 + R_{p2} = 6 + 6 = 12 \, \Omega$
The new total current is:
$I' = \dfrac{12 \text{ V}}{12 \, \Omega} = 1 \text{ A}$
The reading of the voltmeter is the voltage across the parallel branch:
$V' = I' \times R_{p2} = 1 \times 6 = 6 \text{ V}$

Answer: $6$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An ideal DC voltage source of $V$ volts is connected to a circuit through a switch. The circuit consists of a $12\ \Omega$ resistor connected in parallel with a second branch. The second branch contains a $2\ \Omega$ resistor connected in series with a parallel combination of two sub-branches: one sub-branch has a $10\ \Omega$ resistor, and the other sub-branch has an uncharged capacitor $C$ in series with a $2.5\ \Omega$ resistor. The switch is closed at $t = 0$. If $I_{0}$ is the current drawn from the battery immediately after closing the switch, and $I_{\infty}$ is the steady-state current drawn from the battery after a long time, then the ratio $\dfrac{I_{0}}{I_{\infty}}$ is ________.
questions.question: An ideal DC voltage source of $V$ volts is connected to a circuit through a switch. The circuit consists of a $12\ \Omega$ resistor connected in parallel with a second branch. The second branch contains a $2\ \Omega$ resistor connected in series with a parallel combination of two sub-branches: one sub-branch has a $10\ \Omega$ resistor, and the other sub-branch has an uncharged capacitor $C$ in series with a $2.5\ \Omega$ resistor. The switch is closed at $t = 0$. If $I_{0}$ is the current drawn from the battery immediately after closing the switch, and $I_{\infty}$ is the steady-state current drawn from the battery after a long time, then the ratio $\dfrac{I_{0}}{I_{\infty}}$ is ________.
questions.solution:
At $t = 0$, the uncharged capacitor acts as a short circuit. The second branch consists of the $2\ \Omega$ resistor in series with the parallel combination of the $10\ \Omega$ and $2.5\ \Omega$ resistors.

The equivalent resistance of this parallel pair is:
$R_{p0} = \dfrac{10 \times 2.5}{10 + 2.5} = \dfrac{25}{12.5} = 2\ \Omega$

The total resistance of the second branch at $t = 0$ is:
$R_{\text{branch2, } 0} = 2 + 2 = 4\ \Omega$

The total equivalent resistance of the circuit at $t = 0$ is the parallel combination of the $12\ \Omega$ resistor and the $4\ \Omega$ branch:
$R_{0} = \dfrac{12 \times 4}{12 + 4} = \dfrac{48}{16} = 3\ \Omega$

The initial current is $I_{0} = \dfrac{V}{3}$.

At steady state ($t \to \infty$), the capacitor is fully charged and acts as an open circuit. No current flows through the $2.5\ \Omega$ resistor.

The second branch now consists only of the $2\ \Omega$ resistor in series with the $10\ \Omega$ resistor:
$R_{\text{branch2, } \infty} = 2 + 10 = 12\ \Omega$

The total equivalent resistance of the circuit at steady state is the parallel combination of the $12\ \Omega$ resistor and the $12\ \Omega$ branch:
$R_{\infty} = \dfrac{12 \times 12}{12 + 12} = 6\ \Omega$

The steady-state current is $I_{\infty} = \dfrac{V}{6}$.

The required ratio is:
$\dfrac{I_{0}}{I_{\infty}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{V}{3}}{\dfrac{V}{6}} = \dfrac{6}{3} = 2$.

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform wire has a resistance of $18 \Omega$ at $0^{\circ}\text{C}$. The temperature coefficient of resistance of the material of the wire is $5 \times 10^{-3} \ ^{\circ}\text{C}^{-1}$. The wire is bent to form an equilateral triangle and the entire arrangement is kept at a temperature of $100^{\circ}\text{C}$. The equivalent resistance across any two vertices of the triangle at this temperature is _____ $\Omega$.
questions.question: A uniform wire has a resistance of $18 \Omega$ at $0^{\circ}\text{C}$. The temperature coefficient of resistance of the material of the wire is $5 \times 10^{-3} \ ^{\circ}\text{C}^{-1}$. The wire is bent to form an equilateral triangle and the entire arrangement is kept at a temperature of $100^{\circ}\text{C}$. The equivalent resistance across any two vertices of the triangle at this temperature is _____ $\Omega$.
questions.solution:
First, we find the total resistance of the wire at $100^{\circ}\text{C}$.

$R_{T} = R_{0}(1 + \alpha \Delta T)$

$R_{100} = 18(1 + 5 \times 10^{-3} \times 100)$

$R_{100} = 18(1 + 0.5) = 27 \Omega$

The wire is bent into an equilateral triangle, so it is divided into three equal parts. The resistance of each side of the triangle at $100^{\circ}\text{C}$ is:

$R_{side} = \dfrac{27}{3} = 9 \Omega$

Across any two vertices, one side is in parallel with the series combination of the other two sides.

Resistance of the series combination $= 9 + 9 = 18 \Omega$.

The equivalent resistance $R_{eq}$ is:

$R_{eq} = \dfrac{9 \times 18}{9 + 18} = \dfrac{162}{27} = 6 \Omega$.

Answer: $6$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A DC circuit has two terminals A and B. A $4 \Omega$ resistor is connected directly between A and B. From terminal A, a $1 \Omega$ resistor connects to a node C. An unknown resistor $R$ connects node C to terminal B. From node C, a $6 \Omega$ resistor connects to a node D. A $10 \Omega$ resistor connects node D to terminal B. Finally, an ideal conducting wire also connects node D directly to terminal B. If the equivalent resistance across terminals A and B is $2 \Omega$, the value of $R$ is ________.
questions.question: A DC circuit has two terminals A and B. A $4 \Omega$ resistor is connected directly between A and B. From terminal A, a $1 \Omega$ resistor connects to a node C. An unknown resistor $R$ connects node C to terminal B. From node C, a $6 \Omega$ resistor connects to a node D. A $10 \Omega$ resistor connects node D to terminal B. Finally, an ideal conducting wire also connects node D directly to terminal B. If the equivalent resistance across terminals A and B is $2 \Omega$, the value of $R$ is ________.
questions.solution:
The ideal conducting wire connects node D directly to terminal B, which means node D is at the same potential as terminal B. This short-circuits the $10 \Omega$ resistor, so no current flows through it.

The $6 \Omega$ resistor, originally connected between C and D, is now effectively connected between C and B. This places it in parallel with the unknown resistor $R$, which is also connected between C and B.

The equivalent resistance of this parallel combination is $R_{CB} = \dfrac{6R}{6+R}$.

This combination is in series with the $1 \Omega$ resistor (connected between A and C). The total resistance of this branch is $R_{branch} = 1 + \dfrac{6R}{6+R}$.

This entire branch is connected in parallel with the $4 \Omega$ resistor across terminals A and B. The total equivalent resistance is given as $2 \Omega$.

Since $4 \Omega$ in parallel with $R_{branch}$ gives $2 \Omega$, we have:
$\dfrac{4 \times R_{branch}}{4 + R_{branch}} = 2 \Rightarrow R_{branch} = 4 \Omega$

Equating the branch resistance:
$1 + \dfrac{6R}{6+R} = 4$
$\dfrac{6R}{6+R} = 3$
$6R = 18 + 3R$
$3R = 18 \Rightarrow R = 6 \Omega$.

Answer: $6$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A galvanometer of resistance $G$ is converted into an ammeter of range $I$ by connecting a shunt of resistance $S$. To double the range of this ammeter to $2I$, an additional resistor $R$ is connected in parallel with the existing shunt. The value of $R$ is:
questions.question: A galvanometer of resistance $G$ is converted into an ammeter of range $I$ by connecting a shunt of resistance $S$. To double the range of this ammeter to $2I$, an additional resistor $R$ is connected in parallel with the existing shunt. The value of $R$ is:
questions.solution:
For the initial ammeter of range $I$, the maximum current $I_g$ through the galvanometer satisfies:

$I = I_g + I_s = I_g + I_g \dfrac{G}{S} = I_g \left(1 + \dfrac{G}{S}\right)$

Let $S_{eq}$ be the new equivalent shunt resistance when $R$ is connected in parallel with $S$. For the new range $2I$, we have:

$2I = I_g \left(1 + \dfrac{G}{S_{eq}}\right)$

Substituting the expression for $I$ into the second equation:

$2 \left(1 + \dfrac{G}{S}\right) = 1 + \dfrac{G}{S_{eq}}$

$2 + \dfrac{2G}{S} = 1 + \dfrac{G}{S_{eq}}$

$\dfrac{G}{S_{eq}} = 1 + \dfrac{2G}{S}$

$\dfrac{1}{S_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{G} + \dfrac{2}{S}$

Since $S_{eq}$ is the parallel combination of $S$ and $R$, we know $\dfrac{1}{S_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{S} + \dfrac{1}{R}$. Thus:

$\dfrac{1}{S} + \dfrac{1}{R} = \dfrac{1}{G} + \dfrac{2}{S}$

$\dfrac{1}{R} = \dfrac{1}{G} + \dfrac{1}{S} = \dfrac{G+S}{GS}$

$R = \dfrac{GS}{G+S}$

Answer: $\dfrac{GS}{G+S}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A total current of $15\text{ mA}$ enters node $A$ of a circuit and splits into two parallel branches that recombine at node $B$. The first branch consists of a resistor $R_1 = 2\text{ k}\Omega$ connected to node $A$ and a resistor $R_2 = 7\text{ k}\Omega$ connected to node $B$, with a node $C$ between them. The second branch consists of a resistor $R_3 = 4\text{ k}\Omega$ connected to node $A$ and a resistor $R_4 = 2\text{ k}\Omega$ connected to node $B$, with a node $D$ between them. A capacitor of capacitance $C = 5\mu\text{F}$ is connected between nodes $C$ and $D$. The steady-state charge on the capacitor is
questions.question: A total current of $15\text{ mA}$ enters node $A$ of a circuit and splits into two parallel branches that recombine at node $B$. The first branch consists of a resistor $R_1 = 2\text{ k}\Omega$ connected to node $A$ and a resistor $R_2 = 7\text{ k}\Omega$ connected to node $B$, with a node $C$ between them. The second branch consists of a resistor $R_3 = 4\text{ k}\Omega$ connected to node $A$ and a resistor $R_4 = 2\text{ k}\Omega$ connected to node $B$, with a node $D$ between them. A capacitor of capacitance $C = 5\mu\text{F}$ is connected between nodes $C$ and $D$. The steady-state charge on the capacitor is
questions.solution:
In steady state, the capacitor acts as an open circuit, so no current flows through the branch containing it. The total current of $15\text{ mA}$ divides between the two main branches.

The equivalent resistance of the first branch is $R_{b1} = R_1 + R_2 = 2\text{ k}\Omega + 7\text{ k}\Omega = 9\text{ k}\Omega$.
The equivalent resistance of the second branch is $R_{b2} = R_3 + R_4 = 4\text{ k}\Omega + 2\text{ k}\Omega = 6\text{ k}\Omega$.

Using the current division rule, the current in the first branch is:

$I_1 = I_{\text{total}} \times \dfrac{R_{b2}}{R_{b1} + R_{b2}} = 15\text{ mA} \times \dfrac{6}{9 + 6} = 6\text{ mA}$

The current in the second branch is:

$I_2 = I_{\text{total}} \times \dfrac{R_{b1}}{R_{b1} + R_{b2}} = 15\text{ mA} \times \dfrac{9}{9 + 6} = 9\text{ mA}$

The potential at node $C$ relative to node $A$ is determined by the voltage drop across $R_1$:

$V_A - V_C = I_1 \times R_1 = 6\text{ mA} \times 2\text{ k}\Omega = 12\text{ V}$

The potential at node $D$ relative to node $A$ is determined by the voltage drop across $R_3$:

$V_A - V_D = I_2 \times R_3 = 9\text{ mA} \times 4\text{ k}\Omega = 36\text{ V}$

The potential difference across the capacitor is:

$V_{CD} = |(V_A - V_C) - (V_A - V_D)| = |12\text{ V} - 36\text{ V}| = 24\text{ V}$

The steady-state charge on the capacitor is:

$Q = C \times V_{CD} = 5\mu\text{F} \times 24\text{ V} = 120\mu\text{C}$

Answer: $120\mu\text{C}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Five resistors are connected between four distinct nodes A, B, C, and D in an electrical circuit. The resistance values are as follows: $3\ \Omega$ between A and B, $6\ \Omega$ between B and C, $6\ \Omega$ between A and D, $12\ \Omega$ between D and C, and $15\ \Omega$ between B and D. A battery of electromotive force $24\ \text{V}$ and internal resistance $2\ \Omega$ is connected across the nodes A and C. The total current drawn from the battery is
questions.question: Five resistors are connected between four distinct nodes A, B, C, and D in an electrical circuit. The resistance values are as follows: $3\ \Omega$ between A and B, $6\ \Omega$ between B and C, $6\ \Omega$ between A and D, $12\ \Omega$ between D and C, and $15\ \Omega$ between B and D. A battery of electromotive force $24\ \text{V}$ and internal resistance $2\ \Omega$ is connected across the nodes A and C. The total current drawn from the battery is
questions.solution:
The circuit described forms a bridge network between nodes A, B, C, and D, with the battery connected across A and C. We check the balance condition of the Wheatstone bridge:
$\dfrac{R_{AB}}{R_{BC}} = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}$
$\dfrac{R_{AD}}{R_{DC}} = \dfrac{6}{12} = \dfrac{1}{2}$
Since the ratios are equal, the bridge is balanced. The resistor between B and D ($15\ \Omega$) carries no current and can be ignored.

The equivalent resistance of the bridge $R_{bridge}$ is calculated by taking the parallel combination of the branch ABC and the branch ADC:
$R_{ABC} = 3 + 6 = 9\ \Omega$
$R_{ADC} = 6 + 12 = 18\ \Omega$
$R_{bridge} = \dfrac{9 \times 18}{9 + 18} = \dfrac{162}{27} = 6\ \Omega$

The total resistance of the circuit includes the internal resistance $r$ of the battery:
$R_{total} = R_{bridge} + r = 6 + 2 = 8\ \Omega$

The total current drawn from the battery is:
$I = \dfrac{V}{R_{total}} = \dfrac{24}{8} = 3\ \text{A}$

Answer: $3\ \text{A}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An $18\ \text{V}$ battery with an internal resistance of $1\ \Omega$ is connected to a parallel combination of two branches. The first branch contains a $4\ \Omega$ resistor in series with an unknown resistor $R$. The second branch contains a $1\ \Omega$ resistor and a $2\ \Omega$ resistor in series. A branch containing a $3\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor in series with a $5\ \Omega$ resistor is connected in parallel across the unknown resistor $R$. If the steady-state charge on the capacitor is $12\ \mu\text{C}$, the value of the unknown resistance $R$ is _____ $\Omega$.
questions.question: An $18\ \text{V}$ battery with an internal resistance of $1\ \Omega$ is connected to a parallel combination of two branches. The first branch contains a $4\ \Omega$ resistor in series with an unknown resistor $R$. The second branch contains a $1\ \Omega$ resistor and a $2\ \Omega$ resistor in series. A branch containing a $3\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor in series with a $5\ \Omega$ resistor is connected in parallel across the unknown resistor $R$. If the steady-state charge on the capacitor is $12\ \mu\text{C}$, the value of the unknown resistance $R$ is _____ $\Omega$.
questions.solution:
In steady state, the capacitor acts as an open circuit, so no current flows through the $5\ \Omega$ resistor in series with it.

The potential difference across the capacitor is $V_C = \dfrac{Q}{C} = \dfrac{12\ \mu\text{C}}{3\ \mu\text{F}} = 4\ \text{V}$.
Since the capacitor branch is connected in parallel across the unknown resistor $R$ and has no current, the voltage across $R$ is also $V_R = 4\ \text{V}$.

The current in the first branch is $I_1 = \dfrac{V_R}{R} = \dfrac{4}{R}$.
The total voltage across the parallel combination is $V_p = I_1 \times (4 + R) = \dfrac{4}{R}(4 + R) = \dfrac{16}{R} + 4$.

The equivalent resistance of the second branch is $R_2 = 1 + 2 = 3\ \Omega$.
The current in the second branch is $I_2 = \dfrac{V_p}{R_2} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{16}{R} + 4\right)$.

The total current in the circuit is $I = I_1 + I_2 = \dfrac{4}{R} + \dfrac{16}{3R} + \dfrac{4}{3} = \dfrac{28}{3R} + \dfrac{4}{3}$.

Applying Kirchhoff's Voltage Law to the entire circuit:
$E = V_p + Ir$
$18 = \left(\dfrac{16}{R} + 4\right) + \left(\dfrac{28}{3R} + \dfrac{4}{3}\right) \times 1$
$18 - 4 - \dfrac{4}{3} = \dfrac{16}{R} + \dfrac{28}{3R}$
$\dfrac{38}{3} = \dfrac{76}{3R}$
$38 = \dfrac{76}{R} \Rightarrow R = 2\ \Omega$.

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A galvanometer gives full scale deflection for a current of $2 \text{ mA}$. It is converted into an ammeter of range $0$ to $10 \text{ mA}$ by connecting a shunt resistance of $5 \, \Omega$. The resistance of the galvanometer coil is:
questions.question: A galvanometer gives full scale deflection for a current of $2 \text{ mA}$. It is converted into an ammeter of range $0$ to $10 \text{ mA}$ by connecting a shunt resistance of $5 \, \Omega$. The resistance of the galvanometer coil is:
questions.solution:
Let the resistance of the galvanometer be $G$.

Given, full scale deflection current, $i_g = 2 \text{ mA}$.
Range of ammeter, $I = 10 \text{ mA}$.
Shunt resistance, $S = 5 \, \Omega$.

The formula for the shunt resistance required to convert a galvanometer into an ammeter is:
$S = \dfrac{i_g \times G}{I - i_g}$

Substituting the given values:
$5 = \dfrac{2 \times G}{10 - 2}$

$5 = \dfrac{2G}{8}$

$5 = \dfrac{G}{4}$

$G = 20 \, \Omega$

Answer: $20 \, \Omega$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a circuit, nodes B and D are connected to an ideal $12\text{ V}$ battery such that B is at a higher potential. Four resistors are connected as follows: $R_{AB} = 6\,\Omega$, $R_{AD} = 3\,\Omega$, $R_{CB} = 3\,\Omega$, and $R_{CD} = 6\,\Omega$. A fifth branch connecting nodes A and C contains a $2\,\Omega$ resistor and a battery of unknown EMF $E$ with its positive terminal connected to node C. If the steady current flowing in the branch from node C to node A is $2\text{ A}$, the value of $E$ (in volts) is ________.
questions.question: In a circuit, nodes B and D are connected to an ideal $12\text{ V}$ battery such that B is at a higher potential. Four resistors are connected as follows: $R_{AB} = 6\,\Omega$, $R_{AD} = 3\,\Omega$, $R_{CB} = 3\,\Omega$, and $R_{CD} = 6\,\Omega$. A fifth branch connecting nodes A and C contains a $2\,\Omega$ resistor and a battery of unknown EMF $E$ with its positive terminal connected to node C. If the steady current flowing in the branch from node C to node A is $2\text{ A}$, the value of $E$ (in volts) is ________.
questions.solution:
Let the potential at node D be $V_D = 0\text{ V}$. Then the potential at node B is $V_B = 12\text{ V}$.

Applying Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL) at node A. The current entering node A from C is $2\text{ A}$:
$\dfrac{V_A - 12}{6} + \dfrac{V_A - 0}{3} = 2$
Multiplying the equation by 6:
$V_A - 12 + 2V_A = 12 \Rightarrow 3V_A = 24 \Rightarrow V_A = 8\text{ V}$.

Applying KCL at node C. The current leaving node C towards A is $2\text{ A}$:
$\dfrac{V_C - 12}{3} + \dfrac{V_C - 0}{6} + 2 = 0$
Multiplying the equation by 6:
$2V_C - 24 + V_C + 12 = 0 \Rightarrow 3V_C = 12 \Rightarrow V_C = 4\text{ V}$.

For the branch from C to A, the potential difference equation is:
$V_C + E - I \times R_{CA} = V_A$
Substituting the known values:
$4 + E - 2 \times 2 = 8$
$E = 8\text{ V}$.

Answer: $8$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a meter bridge experiment, a resistance of $20 \Omega$ is connected in the left gap and a resistance of $30 \Omega$ is connected in the right gap. To shift the balance point to exactly the center of the bridge wire ($50 \text{ cm}$ from the left end), an unknown resistance $X$ is connected in parallel with the $30 \Omega$ resistance. The value of $X$ is ______ $\Omega$.
questions.question: In a meter bridge experiment, a resistance of $20 \Omega$ is connected in the left gap and a resistance of $30 \Omega$ is connected in the right gap. To shift the balance point to exactly the center of the bridge wire ($50 \text{ cm}$ from the left end), an unknown resistance $X$ is connected in parallel with the $30 \Omega$ resistance. The value of $X$ is ______ $\Omega$.
questions.solution:
For the balance point to be at $50 \text{ cm}$, the effective resistance in the left gap must be equal to the effective resistance in the right gap.

Let the effective resistance in the right gap be $R_{\text{eff}}$.

$\dfrac{20}{R_{\text{eff}}} = \dfrac{50}{100 - 50} = 1$

$R_{\text{eff}} = 20 \Omega$

Since $X$ is connected in parallel with the $30 \Omega$ resistance, we have:

$\dfrac{1}{R_{\text{eff}}} = \dfrac{1}{30} + \dfrac{1}{X}$

$\dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{1}{30} + \dfrac{1}{X}$

$\dfrac{1}{X} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{3 - 2}{60} = \dfrac{1}{60}$

$X = 60 \Omega$

Answer: $60$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wire frame forms a square $ABCD$ with a center point $O$. Eight resistors, each of resistance $R$, are connected: four along the perimeter sides ($AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DA$) and four along the radial segments from the vertices to the center ($OA$, $OB$, $OC$, $OD$). The equivalent resistance between the opposite vertices $A$ and $C$ is
questions.question: A wire frame forms a square $ABCD$ with a center point $O$. Eight resistors, each of resistance $R$, are connected: four along the perimeter sides ($AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DA$) and four along the radial segments from the vertices to the center ($OA$, $OB$, $OC$, $OD$). The equivalent resistance between the opposite vertices $A$ and $C$ is
questions.solution:
Let a voltage be applied across the opposite vertices $A$ and $C$.

The diagonal $BD$ forms an axis of symmetry for the circuit. Due to this symmetry, the nodes $B$, $O$, and $D$ are at the same equipotential state ($V_B = V_O = V_D$).

Because there is no potential difference between $O$ and $B$, and between $O$ and $D$, no current flows through the radial resistors $OB$ and $OD$. These two resistors can be removed from the circuit without affecting the equivalent resistance.

After removing $OB$ and $OD$, the circuit simplifies to three parallel paths connected between $A$ and $C$:
1. Path $A \rightarrow B \rightarrow C$ with resistance $R + R = 2R$
2. Path $A \rightarrow O \rightarrow C$ with resistance $R + R = 2R$
3. Path $A \rightarrow D \rightarrow C$ with resistance $R + R = 2R$

The equivalent resistance $R_{eq}$ is the parallel combination of these three paths:
$\dfrac{1}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{2R} + \dfrac{1}{2R} + \dfrac{1}{2R} = \dfrac{3}{2R}$

$\Rightarrow R_{eq} = \dfrac{2R}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2 R}{3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A galvanometer having a coil resistance of $50 \Omega$ is shunted by a resistance of $2 \Omega$ to convert it into an ammeter. If the maximum current this ammeter can measure is $5.2 \text{ A}$, the current required for full-scale deflection of the original galvanometer is
questions.question: A galvanometer having a coil resistance of $50 \Omega$ is shunted by a resistance of $2 \Omega$ to convert it into an ammeter. If the maximum current this ammeter can measure is $5.2 \text{ A}$, the current required for full-scale deflection of the original galvanometer is
questions.solution:
Let $I_g$ be the current required for full-scale deflection of the galvanometer, $G$ be the galvanometer resistance, $S$ be the shunt resistance, and $I$ be the maximum current to be measured.

The potential difference across the galvanometer and the shunt must be equal:
$I_g G = (I - I_g) S$

Rearranging the terms to solve for $I_g$:
$I_g (G + S) = I S$
$I_g = \dfrac{I S}{G + S}$

Substituting the given values ($G = 50 \Omega$, $S = 2 \Omega$, $I = 5.2 \text{ A}$):
$I_g = \dfrac{5.2 \times 2}{50 + 2}$
$I_g = \dfrac{10.4}{52}$
$I_g = 0.2 \text{ A}$

Converting to milliamperes:
$I_g = 0.2 \times 1000 \text{ mA} = 200 \text{ mA}$

Answer: $200 \text{ mA}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Four resistors are connected to form a Wheatstone bridge ABCD. The resistances of the arms are $R_{AB} = 15\ \Omega$, $R_{BC} = 45\ \Omega$, $R_{AD} = 20\ \Omega$, and $R_{DC} = S$. The bridge is found to be balanced. The resistor $S$ is made of a wire which has a resistance of $25\ \Omega$ at $20^\circ\text{C}$ and a temperature coefficient of resistance $\alpha = 0.02\ ^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$. The temperature of the wire $S$ is ____ $^\circ\text{C}$.
questions.question: Four resistors are connected to form a Wheatstone bridge ABCD. The resistances of the arms are $R_{AB} = 15\ \Omega$, $R_{BC} = 45\ \Omega$, $R_{AD} = 20\ \Omega$, and $R_{DC} = S$. The bridge is found to be balanced. The resistor $S$ is made of a wire which has a resistance of $25\ \Omega$ at $20^\circ\text{C}$ and a temperature coefficient of resistance $\alpha = 0.02\ ^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$. The temperature of the wire $S$ is ____ $^\circ\text{C}$.
questions.solution:
For a balanced Wheatstone bridge, the ratio of resistances in the arms must satisfy:
$\dfrac{R_{AB}}{R_{BC}} = \dfrac{R_{AD}}{R_{DC}}$

Substituting the given values:
$\dfrac{15}{45} = \dfrac{20}{S}$
$\dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{20}{S} \Rightarrow S = 60\ \Omega$

The resistance of the wire $S$ at temperature $T$ is given by:
$S = S_0 [1 + \alpha (T - T_0)]$

Substituting the known values ($S_0 = 25\ \Omega$ at $T_0 = 20^\circ\text{C}$):
$60 = 25 [1 + 0.02 (T - 20)]$
$\dfrac{60}{25} = 1 + 0.02 (T - 20)$
$2.4 = 1 + 0.02 (T - 20)$
$1.4 = 0.02 (T - 20)$
$T - 20 = \dfrac{1.4}{0.02} = 70$
$T = 90^\circ\text{C}$

Answer: $90$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A galvanometer with a coil resistance of $50 \Omega$ requires a shunt resistance of $0.5 \Omega$ to function as an ammeter that can read currents up to $1.01 \mathrm{~A}$. The value of the series resistance required to convert this same galvanometer into a voltmeter that can read up to $5 \mathrm{~V}$ is :
questions.question: A galvanometer with a coil resistance of $50 \Omega$ requires a shunt resistance of $0.5 \Omega$ to function as an ammeter that can read currents up to $1.01 \mathrm{~A}$. The value of the series resistance required to convert this same galvanometer into a voltmeter that can read up to $5 \mathrm{~V}$ is :
questions.solution:
Let the full-scale deflection current of the galvanometer be $\mathrm{I}_{g}$.

For the ammeter conversion:
$\mathrm{I}_{g} \mathrm{R}_{g} = (\mathrm{I} - \mathrm{I}_{g}) \mathrm{S}$
$\mathrm{I}_{g} \times 50 = (1.01 - \mathrm{I}_{g}) \times 0.5$
$50 \mathrm{I}_{g} = 0.505 - 0.5 \mathrm{I}_{g}$
$50.5 \mathrm{I}_{g} = 0.505$
$\mathrm{I}_{g} = 0.01 \mathrm{~A}$

For the voltmeter conversion:
$\mathrm{V} = \mathrm{I}_{g} (\mathrm{R}_{g} + \mathrm{R}_{s})$
$5 = 0.01 (50 + \mathrm{R}_{s})$
$500 = 50 + \mathrm{R}_{s}$
$\mathrm{R}_{s} = 450 \Omega$

Answer: $450 \Omega$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a meter bridge experiment, two unknown resistances $R_1$ and $R_2$ are connected in the left and right gaps respectively. When the positions of $R_1$ and $R_2$ are interchanged, the balance point shifts by $40\text{ cm}$. If the equivalent resistance of $R_1$ and $R_2$ connected in series is $100\ \Omega$ and $R_1 > R_2$, the value of $R_1$ is _____ $\Omega$.
questions.question: In a meter bridge experiment, two unknown resistances $R_1$ and $R_2$ are connected in the left and right gaps respectively. When the positions of $R_1$ and $R_2$ are interchanged, the balance point shifts by $40\text{ cm}$. If the equivalent resistance of $R_1$ and $R_2$ connected in series is $100\ \Omega$ and $R_1 > R_2$, the value of $R_1$ is _____ $\Omega$.
questions.solution:
Let the initial balance point from the left end be $l$.

Since $R_1 > R_2$, the initial balance point $l > 50\text{ cm}$.

The balance condition is:
$\dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \dfrac{l}{100 - l}$

When $R_1$ and $R_2$ are interchanged, the new balance point $l'$ from the left end will be $100 - l$.

The shift in the balance point is given as $40\text{ cm}$.
$\Rightarrow l - (100 - l) = 40$
$\Rightarrow 2l - 100 = 40$
$\Rightarrow 2l = 140 \Rightarrow l = 70\text{ cm}$

Now, substituting $l = 70\text{ cm}$ in the balance condition:
$\dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \dfrac{70}{100 - 70} = \dfrac{7}{3}$
$\Rightarrow R_2 = \dfrac{3}{7}R_1$

Given that the series combination $R_1 + R_2 = 100\ \Omega$:
$R_1 + \dfrac{3}{7}R_1 = 100$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{10}{7}R_1 = 100$
$\Rightarrow R_1 = 70\ \Omega$

Answer: $70$

questions.q: A battery of emf $25 \text{ V}$ and internal resistance $1 \Omega$ is connected across two terminals A and B of a resistor network. A $20 \Omega$ resistor is connected directly between A and B. From terminal A, a $2 \Omega$ resistor connects to a node C. A $6 \Omega$ resistor connects node C to terminal B. From node C, a $4 \Omega$ resistor connects to a node D. A $3 \Omega$ resistor connects node D to terminal B. From node D, a $6 \Omega$ resistor connects to a node E. An $8 \Omega$ resistor connects node E to terminal B. Finally, a thick conducting wire connects node E directly to terminal B. The power dissipated in the $4 \Omega$ resistor is ________ W.
questions.question: A battery of emf $25 \text{ V}$ and internal resistance $1 \Omega$ is connected across two terminals A and B of a resistor network. A $20 \Omega$ resistor is connected directly between A and B. From terminal A, a $2 \Omega$ resistor connects to a node C. A $6 \Omega$ resistor connects node C to terminal B. From node C, a $4 \Omega$ resistor connects to a node D. A $3 \Omega$ resistor connects node D to terminal B. From node D, a $6 \Omega$ resistor connects to a node E. An $8 \Omega$ resistor connects node E to terminal B. Finally, a thick conducting wire connects node E directly to terminal B. The power dissipated in the $4 \Omega$ resistor is ________ W.
questions.solution:
The thick conducting wire connects node E directly to terminal B, short-circuiting the $8 \Omega$ resistor. Thus, node E is at the same potential as terminal B.

The $6 \Omega$ resistor (between D and E) is now effectively connected between D and B. This places it in parallel with the $3 \Omega$ resistor (also between D and B).
Equivalent resistance between D and B: $R_{DB} = \dfrac{3 \times 6}{3 + 6} = 2 \Omega$.

This $2 \Omega$ equivalent is in series with the $4 \Omega$ resistor (between C and D), making the resistance of the branch C-D-B equal to $4 + 2 = 6 \Omega$.

This $6 \Omega$ branch is in parallel with the $6 \Omega$ resistor connected directly between C and B.
Equivalent resistance between C and B: $R_{CB} = \dfrac{6 \times 6}{6 + 6} = 3 \Omega$.

This $3 \Omega$ equivalent is in series with the $2 \Omega$ resistor (between A and C). The total resistance of the right branch across A and B is $2 + 3 = 5 \Omega$.

This $5 \Omega$ branch is in parallel with the $20 \Omega$ resistor across A and B.
Total external resistance: $R_{ext} = \dfrac{20 \times 5}{20 + 5} = 4 \Omega$.

Total resistance of the circuit including the battery's internal resistance is $R_{tot} = 4 + 1 = 5 \Omega$.
Total current drawn from the battery: $I_{tot} = \dfrac{25}{5} = 5 \text{ A}$.

Terminal voltage across A and B: $V_{AB} = E - I_{tot}r = 25 - 5(1) = 20 \text{ V}$.

Current flowing into the right branch (A-C-B): $I_{branch} = \dfrac{20}{5} = 4 \text{ A}$.

At node C, this $4 \text{ A}$ current splits into two parallel paths (C-B directly and C-D-B), both having a resistance of $6 \Omega$. The current splits equally, so the current through the C-D-B path is $2 \text{ A}$.

This $2 \text{ A}$ current flows through the $4 \Omega$ resistor. The power dissipated in it is:
$P = I^2 R = (2)^2 \times 4 = 16 \text{ W}$.

Answer: $16$

questions.q: Two cells, one of EMF $12\text{ V}$ and internal resistance $1\Omega$ and another of unknown EMF $E$ ($E < 12\text{ V}$) and internal resistance $2\Omega$, are connected in series such that their positive terminals are joined together. This combination is connected across an external circuit consisting of a $3\Omega$ resistor in series with a parallel combination of a $4\Omega$ and a $12\Omega$ resistor. If the current flowing through the $4\Omega$ resistor is $0.75\text{ A}$, the value of $E$ (in Volts) is ________.
questions.question: Two cells, one of EMF $12\text{ V}$ and internal resistance $1\Omega$ and another of unknown EMF $E$ ($E < 12\text{ V}$) and internal resistance $2\Omega$, are connected in series such that their positive terminals are joined together. This combination is connected across an external circuit consisting of a $3\Omega$ resistor in series with a parallel combination of a $4\Omega$ and a $12\Omega$ resistor. If the current flowing through the $4\Omega$ resistor is $0.75\text{ A}$, the value of $E$ (in Volts) is ________.
questions.solution:
The equivalent resistance of the parallel combination of $4\Omega$ and $12\Omega$ resistors is:
$R_p = \dfrac{4 \times 12}{4 + 12} = \dfrac{48}{16} = 3\Omega$

The total external resistance of the circuit is:
$R_{ext} = 3\Omega + 3\Omega = 6\Omega$

The total resistance of the entire circuit, including the internal resistances of the cells, is:
$R_{total} = R_{ext} + r_1 + r_2 = 6 + 1 + 2 = 9\Omega$

Let the total current in the main circuit be $I$. Using the current divider rule, the current through the $4\Omega$ resistor is:
$I_4 = I \times \dfrac{12}{4 + 12} = I \times \dfrac{12}{16} = I \times \dfrac{3}{4}$

Given that $I_4 = 0.75\text{ A}$, we have:
$0.75 = I \times 0.75 \Rightarrow I = 1\text{ A}$

Since the positive terminals of the cells are joined together, they are connected in opposition. The net EMF of the circuit is:
$E_{net} = 12 - E$

Using Ohm's law for the complete circuit:
$I = \dfrac{E_{net}}{R_{total}}$
$1 = \dfrac{12 - E}{9}$
$9 = 12 - E$
$E = 3\text{ V}$

Answer: $3$

questions.q: A circuit consists of two sections connected in series. Section A has two identical resistors, each of resistance $xR_0$, connected in parallel. Section B consists of a single resistor of resistance $\dfrac{8R_0}{x}$. Here $x$ is a variable positive parameter and $R_0$ is a constant resistance. If the minimum possible equivalent resistance of the entire circuit is $48\Omega$, the value of $R_0$ is _____ $\Omega$.
questions.question: A circuit consists of two sections connected in series. Section A has two identical resistors, each of resistance $xR_0$, connected in parallel. Section B consists of a single resistor of resistance $\dfrac{8R_0}{x}$. Here $x$ is a variable positive parameter and $R_0$ is a constant resistance. If the minimum possible equivalent resistance of the entire circuit is $48\Omega$, the value of $R_0$ is _____ $\Omega$.
questions.solution:
The equivalent resistance of Section A, which has two identical resistors in parallel, is:

$R_A = \dfrac{xR_0}{2}$

The resistance of Section B is:

$R_B = \dfrac{8R_0}{x}$

Since Section A and Section B are connected in series, the total equivalent resistance $R_{\text{eq}}$ of the circuit is:

$R_{\text{eq}} = R_A + R_B = \dfrac{xR_0}{2} + \dfrac{8R_0}{x}$

To find the minimum value of $R_{\text{eq}}$, we can use the AM-GM inequality for the two positive terms:

$\dfrac{\dfrac{xR_0}{2} + \dfrac{8R_0}{x}}{2} \ge \sqrt{\dfrac{xR_0}{2} \times \dfrac{8R_0}{x}}$

$R_{\text{eq}} \ge 2\sqrt{4R_0^2} = 4R_0$

Thus, the minimum possible equivalent resistance is $4R_0$. We are given that this minimum resistance is $48\Omega$.

$4R_0 = 48$

$R_0 = 12$

Answer: $12$
